title: SLO Observability Fidelity and Instrumentation Specification
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview
========

Purpose: Define a standardized, cost-aware observability "fidelity" model and concrete instrumentation requirements so SREs and service owners can map SLOs and error-budget policies to telemetry collection, retention, and alerting. This spec balances operational signal, cost, and privacy across Redwood's multi-tenant model-serving platform.

Intended audience: SREs, service owners, infra engineers, instrumentation engineers, and product security reviewers.

Goals
-----
- Provide a small, actionable taxonomy of telemetry fidelity levels (Coarse, Standard, High) and when to use each.
- Specify required metric names, labels, and log/event schema for model-serving services and control planes.
- Define sampling, retention, and indexing guidance tied to SLO classes and error-budget consumption.
- Prescribe rollout steps, verification queries, and ownership for new instrumentation.

Scope
-----
Applies to all services that contribute to production SLOs for model inference (hosted API, dedicated clusters, private deployments orchestrated by Redwood). This includes: request path, routing, batching, KV cache hits, GPU scheduling, model quantization variants, and dependency calls (e.g., KMS, storage). It does not replace service-level logging practices but augments them with SLO-aligned telemetry.

Telemetry Fidelity Taxonomy
--------------------------
1) Coarse (default for low-criticality services)
   - Purpose: long-term cost-efficient trend analysis and capacity forecasting.
   - Metrics: per-minute aggregated counters and histograms at service-level (no tenant dimension).
   - Typical retention: 365d for aggregates, 90d for histograms.
   - When to use: non-customer-facing batch jobs, auxiliary internal services, or when cost must be minimized.

2) Standard (default for most model-serving paths)
   - Purpose: support SLO compliance, alerting, and fast triage for customer-impacting issues.
   - Metrics: per-tenant and per-route latency histograms, error counters, concurrency, queue length, and cache hit-rate.
   - Typical retention: 90d for all metric series, 30d for high-cardinality labels (see cardinality policy).
   - When to use: production inference endpoints, routing/proxy layers, autoscalers.

3) High (for active incidents, postmortems, or deep perf tuning)
   - Purpose: detailed root-cause analysis and model-of-record investigation.
   - Metrics & traces: full request traces (sampling up to 100% for a limited window), per-tenant per-model sampling, and more granular GPU/worker-level telemetry.
   - Typical retention: 30d for full traces; 90d for derived aggregates.
   - When to use: while diagnosing SLO regressions, during canary rollouts of new model weights/quantization, or for enterprise customers under SLA investigation.

Decision rules: promote fidelity to High automatically when
- SLO error budget burn rate > 4x sustained for 1h, OR
- Active incident label=severity>=P1 and SLO owner enables full-trace capture.
Demote back to Standard after a configurable cooldown (default 72h) unless manual hold requested.

Required Metric Taxonomy (naming conventions)
-------------------------------------------
All metric names follow the prefix redwood.<service>.<signal>.<aggregation>. Use snake_case for labels. Examples: 
- redwood.api.request.latency_ms.p50
- redwood.api.request.latency_ms.p95
- redwood.api.request.errors.rate
- redwood.kvcache.hit_rate
- redwood.inference.kv_cache.size
- redwood.inference.gpu.utilization
- redwood.routing.queue_length

Mandatory labels (where applicable):
- service: logical service name (e.g., api, routing, runtime)
- region: cloud region or on-prem site
- model_id: model identifier (short name, version tag)
- route: API surface or route name
- tenant_id: obfuscated tenant id (hash) — never use raw customer PII
- quantization: {fp16, int8, q4_0, q4_1, none}

Cardinality policy:
- tenant_id: allowed for Standard fidelity but only for top N tenants by traffic (see Top-Tenant Sampling below).
- model_id: required for all model-serving histograms.
- route: required for SLO-linked metrics.
- Avoid freeform labels (e.g., raw file names, user agent strings) without bucketing.

Sampling and Top-Tenant Strategy
-------------------------------
To control cardinality and cost:
1) Define Top N tenants per service (default N=200) kept at full sampling.
2) For the long tail, use 1/100 sampling of tenant_id and expose aggregated buckets: long_tail_bucket=(0-0.1%, 0.1-1%, 1-5%, 5-20%).
3) For High fidelity mode, temporarily raise sampling to 100% for affected tenants or routes for windows defined by the incident.

Example: Prometheus-style recording rule (Standard fidelity p95)
----------------------------------------------------------------
# record p95 per service+route+model (aggregates; avoid per-tenant for long tail)
- record: redwood:request_latency_ms:95
  expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_api_request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (service, route, model_id))

Instrumentation Requirements by Signal
-------------------------------------
1) Request Path\   - Emit: request_start, request_end events with request_id, tenant_id hash, model_id, route, outcome (success|error|timeout), tokens_in, tokens_out.
  - Metrics derived: latency histograms (ms), error rates, tokens/sec.
  - Trace spans: include model_load_span, kv_cache_lookup, kernel_exec where available.

2) KV Cache
  - Emit: kv_lookup, kv_hit, kv_miss counters with model_id and cache_key_bucket (hash bucket).
  - Derived: hit_rate = hits / (hits+misses) over 1m window. SLOs reference hit_rate thresholds per workload class.

3) Batching & Scheduling
  - Emit: batch_size distribution, batch_delay_ms histogram, worker_queue_length.
  - Derived SLO signal: p95(batch_delay_ms) < configured threshold for low-latency routes.

4) GPU & Worker health
  - Emit: gpu_util_pct, gpu_memory_free_mb, worker_oom_count, worker_restart_count. Alert when gpu_util_pct sustained > 95% and queue length rising.

Alert Mapping & SLO Integration
------------------------------
SLO Classes (example):
- Gold: p95_latency < 150ms, availability >= 99.95%
- Silver: p95_latency < 300ms, availability >= 99.9%
- Bronze: p95_latency < 800ms, availability >= 99.5%

Alerting guidance:
1) Burn-rate alerts (SREs): trigger when 6h rolling burn rate > 2x expected or 1h burn rate > 4x.
2) Symptom alerts (oncall): latency/error thresholds tied to routes and per-region SLOs (eg: p95_latency(region,route) > threshold for 5m).
3) Early-warning capacity alerts (ops): queue_length or gpu_utilization patterns that predict SLO violations (use predictive anomaly detection where available).

Each alert must include: affected SLO id, current error-budget remaining percentage, suggested mitigation (eg: enable model-variant fallback, reduce batching window, spill to dedicated pool).

Runbook & Execution Triggers for Fidelity Changes
-------------------------------------------------
Automated triggers (system):
- If burn-rate > 4x sustained 1h => auto-escalate fidelity for affected routes to High for 2h window and notify SREs.
- If predictive capacity model projects >50% probability of SLO breach in next 30m => increase fidelity for impacted tenants and enable sampling for traces.

Manual runbook steps (SRE oncall) to enable High fidelity for a route:
1) Identify route/service and confirm SLO id and owner.
2) From the observability console run: `rwd telemetry-fidelity set --service <service> --route <route> --fidelity high --window 120m --reason "<incident-id>"`
3) Update incident ticket with sampling scope and ETA for demotion.
4) After diagnostics, demote fidelity with: `rwd telemetry-fidelity set --service <service> --route <route> --fidelity standard` and record rationale.

Rollout & Verification Checklist for New Instrumentation
--------------------------------------------------------
1) Instrumentation review: add CHANGELOG entry + PR linking to this spec. Reviewer: telemetry-owner.
2) Unit tests: metric emitted on happy path and error path.
3) Canary: enable Standard fidelity instrumentation in canary region for 48h.
4) Verification queries to run post-rollout:
   - `sum(rate(redwood.api.request.errors[5m])) by (service,route)` -> should not spike due to instrumentation.
   - Check cardinality: `count(count by (tenant_id) (redwood_api_request_total{tenant_id!=""}[1h]))` must be <= Top N + margin.
5) Cost impact review: estimate additional unique series and storage delta. Approvals required if >+5% monthly telemetry cost.

Ownership and Maintenance
-------------------------
- telemetry-owner (team-level): responsible for instrumentation PR reviews, maintaining recording rules, and responding to fidelity escalations.
- SLO owner: defines mapping of SLO class to default fidelity and approves High fidelity usage for their service.
- Observability platform (eng-platform): enforces cardinality caps and automates Top-Tenant lists nightly.

Observability Security & Privacy Constraints
-------------------------------------------
- tenant_id must be a stable hash (SHA256 truncated) with no reversible mapping stored in telemetry storage.
- No raw customer PII (email, org name) in labels or logs that feed into metric series. Use audit logs with tighter access controls for PII.

Appendix A — Example PromQL Recipes
----------------------------------
- p95 per service and route (5m sliding):
  `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_api_request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (service, route))`
- error budget remaining (example):
  `1 - (sum(rate(redwood_api_request_errors_total[30d])) / sum(rate(redwood_api_requests_total[30d])))`
- burn rate (1h vs 30d baseline):
  `sum(rate(redwood_api_request_errors_total[1h])) / (sum(rate(redwood_api_request_errors_total[30d])) / (30*24))`

Appendix B — Log / Event Schema (newline-delimited JSON)
------------------------------------------------------
Required fields for request_end event:
- timestamp (ISO8601)
- request_id (uuid)
- service, route, region, model_id
- tenant_hash
- status (OK|ERROR|TIMEOUT)
- latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out
- error_code (optional)

Example event:
{
  "timestamp": "2025-03-02T17:24:33.512Z",
  "request_id": "3f9b27a6-....",
  "service": "api",
  "route": "/v1/generate",
  "region": "us-west-2",
  "model_id": "redwood-llama-13b-v2",
  "tenant_hash": "a1b2c3d4",
  "status": "OK",
  "latency_ms": 87,
  "tokens_in": 24,
  "tokens_out": 128
}
